ai.description: *Minervarya pentali* is a small frog (25–30 mm) with a brown dorsum and distinct reddish-brown patches. It features a prominent, continuous mid-dorsal ridge and a pair of distinct, dark-colored supratympanic folds.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Minervarya pentali* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous, and prominent white mid-dorsal stripe running from the snout to the vent.
ai.habitat: *Minervarya pentali* inhabits the Western Ghats, typically found in moist deciduous forests and riparian zones at elevations between 500 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: *Minervarya pentali* is primarily nocturnal, emerging after dark to forage for small insects and invertebrates among the leaf litter of the Western Ghats.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Minervarya pentali* breeds during the monsoon, laying clutches of 100–300 eggs in shallow water bodies. It follows an aquatic larval development cycle.
ai.distributionRemarks: Minervarya pentali is endemic to the southern Western Ghats, primarily occurring in the states of Kerala and Karnataka at elevations between 200 and 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Minervarya pentali* consists of a series of rapid, high-pitched "ticking" notes, typically heard from shallow, rain-filled puddles in forest habitats.
